body:
https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/actions/runs/26700756599/job/78693107792 

can we detect it; and how do we fix it automatically ? @sepo-agent /answer

comments.body:
Yes. The linked job is a clean example: `Run agent` started at `02:11:09` and was killed at `02:41:22`, matching the default 30 minute task timeout. GitHub emitted `The action has timed out.`

What exists today:

- Sepo already has an outer per-route GitHub Actions timeout via `AGENT_TASK_TIMEOUT_POLICY`.
  - Resolver: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/task-timeout-policy.ts#L1
  - Docs: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/docs/customization/configuration-list.md#L30
  - `fix-pr` wiring: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-fix-pr.yml#L172-L184
- The current failure classification is generic. `fix-pr` maps any failed agent step to `AGENT_EXIT_CODE=1`, then `determineRunStatus()` returns only `failed`, not `timed_out`.
  - https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-fix-pr.yml#L233-L242
  - https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/response.ts#L13-L30
- The inner acpx adapter already has timeout plumbing, but `run.ts` does not pass a timeout into `runAcpx()`.
  - Existing adapter support: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/acpx-adapter.ts#L21-L40
  - Passed to acpx/spawn when set: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/acpx-adapter.ts#L756-L776
  - Current caller omits it: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/run.ts#L560-L578

So: **we can detect it today in logs/API, but Sepo does not yet classify it as a first-class timeout outcome inside the agent status model.**

Immediate mitigation: set a larger repo variable, for example:

```json
{"default_minutes":30,"route_overrides":{"fix-pr":60,"implement":60,"orchestrate":45}}
```

That is useful, but not a real automatic fix.

Recommended implementation plan:

1. Add an inner agent timeout that is slightly below the GitHub step timeout, e.g. `resolved_minutes * 60 - 60`.
2. Pass that value into `run-agent-task` and then into `.agent/src/run.ts`.
3. Have `runAcpx()` return a typed timeout result when `spawnSync` times out or when acpx exits due to `--timeout`.
4. Add a new run status, likely `timed_out`, alongside `failed`.
5. Update `parse-response`, `post-comment`, `implement`, `fix-pr`, `answer`, and orchestrator handoff wiring so timeouts are visible as timeouts, not generic failures.
6. For automatic recovery:
   - If session identity is available, back up/register it and resume the same route.
   - If identity is unavailable, redispatch the same route once with a longer timeout or reduced reasoning effort/model policy.
   - Cap retries with the existing automation round controls so this cannot loop forever.
7. Add regression tests around `acpx-adapter`, `parse-response`, and workflow rendering.

I’d implement the inner timeout/classification first, then add retry policy as a second pass. That keeps the first change small and makes future automation deterministic instead of log-scraping GitHub’s timeout message.

---
`codex` | `gpt-5.5/medium` | `high` | `Macmini-runner-2`
@sepo-agent /answer I do wonder if people complain about this issue inside acpx repo -- can you search

I searched. I don’t see strong evidence that this exact Sepo/GitHub Actions failure is a widely reported `openclaw/acpx` repo issue, but there are several adjacent reports around **Codex + ACP/acpx wrappers + timeouts/stalls**.

Relevant findings:

- `openclaw/acpx` itself is explicitly alpha, and it already exposes timeout controls: `--timeout 1800`, `--timeout 90`, plus config `"timeout": null` by default. So acpx has a timeout surface we can use from Sepo. Source: https://github.com/openclaw/acpx
- OpenAI Codex has open timeout complaints around shell/tool commands, sandboxing, and commands returning timeout/exit 124. Example: openai/codex#7353, “Codex commands timeout issue,” including reports that every command times out under some shell/sandbox setups. Source: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/7353
- OpenClaw has a very close architectural issue: Codex app-server turns timing out after 60s despite meaningful progress. The proposed fix there is exactly the shape I’d use here: separate request timeout from turn hard cap, make progress refresh the idle window, and keep a terminal hard cap. Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78756
- OpenClaw also has an ACP/Codex long-running-session issue where `sessions_send` returns `timeout` after 30s even though the target ACP/Codex session is actively working, because the caller lacks progress visibility. Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/54895
- There are reports of ACP + Codex sessions silently stalling or failing to report completion/timeout/cleanup. Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/29195
- There are also ACP spawn-path hangs where direct acpx works, but the higher-level OpenClaw spawn path hangs. That suggests some timeout/stall cases are wrapper/orchestration bugs, not acpx itself. Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/51345

My read: this supports fixing Sepo locally rather than waiting upstream. The linked Sepo failure was the GitHub Actions outer 30m timeout killing `Run agent`; that is not enough evidence of an acpx bug. But upstream reports do validate the design concern: wrappers need typed timeout detection, progress-aware waiting, and bounded retry/resume.

Concrete next step for Sepo: pass an inner timeout to `acpx --timeout` slightly below the Actions `timeout-minutes`, classify timeout separately from generic failure, then retry/resume once with a larger budget or lower reasoning setting.
